intro: The Bible is full of people who had to be brave. In this unit you will meet a shepherd boy with a sling, a man in a den of lions, and a man inside a big fish. These stories come from the Old Testament, which Jews and Christians both read.

Then you will meet a teacher named Jesus. Christians tell his story from the New Testament. He taught with short stories called parables. You will hear about a lost sheep, a tiny seed and a hurt man on a road.
By the end, you will be able to tell each story in order, say who is in it, and say what a psalm, a prophet and a parable are. You will also learn what Christians remember at Christmas and Easter.
bigQuestion: What do these stories say about being brave and being kind?

timeline.t: David watches his family's sheep near Bethlehem
David faces the giant Goliath with a sling
David becomes king and makes Jerusalem his city
Songs called psalms carry David's name
Daniel prays and is thrown to the lions
Jonah runs away, meets a big fish, and goes to Nineveh
Luke and Matthew tell of a baby born in Bethlehem
Jesus teaches with parables like the lost sheep
Jesus tells the story of the Good Samaritan
Jesus welcomes the children his helpers sent away
Christians remember Jesus at Christmas and Easter

words.d: a person who watches sheep and keeps them safe
a strip of cloth or leather used to throw a stone fast
a song or poem from the Bible's book of Psalms
a person in the Bible who speaks a message the text says comes from God
doing the right thing even when you feel scared
one of four books that tell the story of Jesus
a short story with a lesson inside
a person near you who you should care about

test.q: What was David's job when he was a boy?
test.why: The story in 1 Samuel says David watched his family's sheep.

test.q: Who did David beat with a sling and a stone?
test.why: The story says David's stone hit the giant Goliath, and he fell.
Psalm 23 begins, "The LORD is my shepherd," and talks about green grass and quiet water.

test.q: Why was Daniel thrown to the lions?
test.why: The story says a rule said not to pray to anyone but the king, and Daniel prayed anyway.

test.q: What did the people of Nineveh do when Jonah spoke?
choices: They threw him in the sea
test.why: The book of Jonah says the whole city said sorry and changed.

choices: A person who speaks a message
test.why: In the Bible, a prophet speaks a message the text says comes from God. Jonah was one.

test.q: Which part of the Bible tells the story of Jesus?
test.why: The New Testament, with its four Gospels, tells the story of Jesus.

test.q: Which Gospel tells about the wise men and the star?
test.why: Matthew has the wise men and the star. Luke has the shepherds and the manger.

test.q: In the Good Samaritan story, what did the Samaritan do?
test.why: The priest and the temple helper walked past. The Samaritan stopped and cared for the man.

test.q: Which of these is a parable?
test.why: The lost sheep is a parable, a short story with a lesson, that the Gospels say Jesus told.

write.prompt: Pick one brave person from this unit: David, Daniel, Jonah or the Samaritan. Tell what the story says he did. Name the book the story is in, like 1 Samuel 17 or Luke 10. Then say why you think it was brave or kind.
tips: Say the book the story comes from.
Say "the story says" when you tell what happened.
Tell what happened in order: first, next, last.
Use a word from this unit, like prophet, psalm or parable.
